98847.subject: Building Construction
98847.question_text:
You are provided with samples of three different building materials: clay bricks, concrete blocks, and timber.

Describe the physical properties of each material that influence their selection for use in wall construction. Include in your answer:
(i) Density
(ii) Thermal conductivity
(iii) Durability
(iv) Workability
98847.explanation:
Clay Bricks:
(i) Density: Moderate density (~1600–2000 kg/m³), providing good load-bearing capacity.
(ii) Thermal conductivity: Low thermal conductivity, offering good insulation.
(iii) Durability: Highly durable, resistant to weathering and fire.
(iv) Workability: Easy to cut and shape but requires skilled labor for bonding.

Concrete Blocks:
(i) Density: Higher density (~1800–2400 kg/m³), suitable for load-bearing walls.
(ii) Thermal conductivity: Higher than bricks, requiring additional insulation.
(iii) Durability: Highly durable, resistant to pests and fire.
(iv) Workability: Easier to handle due to larger size but heavier.

Timber:
(i) Density: Low density (~400–800 kg/m³), lightweight but limited load-bearing capacity.
(ii) Thermal conductivity: Low, providing excellent insulation.
(iii) Durability: Susceptible to rot, pests, and fire unless treated.
(iv) Workability: Highly workable, easy to cut and shape.

98848.subject: Building Construction
98848.question_text: Which of the following factors is LEAST important when selecting materials for constructing a load-bearing wall in a residential building in Ghana?
98848.explanation: The least important factor for load-bearing walls is aesthetic appeal, as structural integrity, durability, and cost are prioritized. Load-bearing walls must support the building's weight, so strength and stability are critical.

98849.subject: Building Construction
98849.question_text:
You are tasked with preparing three types of mortar for different construction purposes. Describe the proportions of materials and suitable applications for each of the following:
(i) Cement mortar
(ii) Lime mortar
(iii) Gauged mortar
98849.explanation:
(i) Cement Mortar:
Proportions: 1 part cement to 3–6 parts sand (depending on strength required).
Applications: Load-bearing walls, foundations, and high-strength masonry.

(ii) Lime Mortar:
Proportions: 1 part lime to 2–3 parts sand.
Applications: Historic buildings, non-load-bearing walls, and restoration work due to flexibility.

(iii) Gauged Mortar:
Proportions: 1 part cement, 1 part lime, and 6 parts sand.
Applications: General masonry work, offering a balance of strength and workability.

98850.subject: Building Construction
98850.question_text: Which type of foundation is most suitable for a two-storey residential building constructed on soft clay soil in Accra?
98850.explanation: A raft foundation is most suitable for soft clay soil as it distributes the building's load evenly, reducing settlement risks. It acts as a single slab covering the entire building footprint.

98851.subject: Building Construction
98851.question_text: Describe the step-by-step procedure for setting out a rectangular building of dimensions 12m × 8m on a construction site. Include the tools required and the checks to ensure accuracy.
98851.explanation:
Tools Required: Theodolite, tape measure, pegs, builder’s square, spirit level, string line.

Procedure:
1. Establish a baseline using the theodolite and pegs.
2. Mark the first corner (A) and measure 12m along the baseline to mark corner B.
3. Use the builder’s square to set a 90° angle at corner A and measure 8m to mark corner D.
4. Repeat at corner B to mark corner C, ensuring the diagonal (A to C) measures $sqrt{12^2 + 8^2} = 14.42m$ for accuracy.
5. Check all angles with the theodolite and adjust pegs as needed.
6. Use string lines to outline the building perimeter.

98852.subject: Building Construction
98852.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a standard safety measure during excavation work?
98852.explanation: Using unshored trenches deeper than 1.5m is unsafe and violates excavation safety standards. Trenches deeper than 1.5m must be shored or sloped to prevent collapse.

options.text: Providing adequate shoring for deep trenches
Providing safe access and egress for workers

98853.subject: Building Construction
98853.question_text:
Sketch and describe the construction details of the following brick bonding patterns:
(i) Stretcher bond
(ii) English bond
(iii) Flemish bond
Include their applications and advantages.
98853.explanation:
(i) Stretcher Bond:
Description: Bricks laid lengthwise with joints staggered by half a brick.
Applications: Non-load-bearing walls, cavity walls.
Advantages: Simple, fast, and economical.

(ii) English Bond:
Description: Alternating courses of headers and stretchers.
Applications: Load-bearing walls.
Advantages: Strong, durable, and aesthetically pleasing.

(iii) Flemish Bond:
Description: Alternating headers and stretchers in the same course.
Applications: Decorative and load-bearing walls.
Advantages: Attractive appearance, good strength.

98854.subject: Building Construction
98854.question_text: Which damp-proofing method is most effective for preventing rising damp in a brick wall?
98854.explanation: A damp-proof course (DPC) is the most effective method for preventing rising damp. It is a horizontal barrier (e.g., bitumen, plastic, or slate) installed in the wall to block moisture from rising through capillary action.

98855.subject: Building Construction
98855.question_text: Explain the role of reinforcement in concrete and describe the steps involved in constructing a reinforced concrete beam. Include the types of reinforcement used and their placement.
98855.explanation:
Role of Reinforcement: Reinforcement (steel bars) resists tensile forces, while concrete resists compression, creating a composite material with high strength.

Steps for Constructing a Reinforced Concrete Beam:
1. Formwork: Erect wooden or metal formwork to shape the beam.
2. Reinforcement: Place main bars (longitudinal) for tension and stirrups (transverse) for shear resistance.
3. Concrete Mixing: Prepare concrete mix (1:2:4 ratio for general use).
4. Placement: Pour concrete into formwork, ensuring full compaction.
5. Curing: Keep moist for 7–14 days to achieve full strength.

98856.subject: Building Construction
98856.question_text: Which roof covering material is most suitable for a low-cost housing project in a rainy region of Ghana?
98856.explanation: Corrugated galvanized iron (CGI) sheets are most suitable for low-cost housing in rainy regions due to their affordability, durability, and waterproof properties. They are also easy to install and maintain.
